card.title: Per-Key Sliding Window Rate Limiter Filter

a1.cap: Protect an AI endpoint: each X-API-Key may make at most 60 requests in any rolling 60 seconds. Extra requests get 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. Implement it as a servlet filter using the sliding-window log idea, safe under concurrent requests.

lines: Protect an AI endpoint: each X-API-Key may make at most 60 requests in any rolling 60 seconds. Extra requests get 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. Implement it as a servlet filter using the sliding-window log idea, safe under concurrent requests.

a1.cap: This is the sliding-window algorithm from the Practice tab, inside a real web filter. Each API key owns a deque of request times. On each request, drop timestamps older than the window from the front; if the deque is still full, reject with 429.
Locking only the key's own deque keeps different clients from blocking each other. In a multi-instance deployment you'd move this state to Redis.
OncePerRequestFilter guarantees the filter runs exactly once per request, before any controller.
a1.say: Once Per Request Filter guarantees the filter runs exactly once per request, before any controller.

a1.cap: Each API key gets its own deque of timestamps in a thread-safe map.
Requests without an API key are rejected with 401 straight away.
computeIfAbsent creates the key's deque atomically on its first request.
a1.say: compute If Absent creates the key's deque atomically on its first request.

a1.cap: We lock only this key's deque, so other clients are never blocked.
Slide the window: drop timestamps that are 60 seconds old or more from the front.
If the window is still full, the client must wait.
Retry-After tells the client exactly when the oldest request leaves the window.
Otherwise record this request and let it continue down the filter chain.
